title: Electric Cell-Substrate Sensing for Real-Time Evaluation of Metal-Organic Framework Toxicological Profiles
protocol: Measure zinc nitrate hexahydrate using a 1:10:100 mass ratio for metal:linker:solvent.
Calculate and measure out 2-methylimidazole based on the calculated amount of zinc nitrate hexahydrate.
Calculate and measure methanol to use half with zinc nitrate hexydrate and half with linker.
Add half of the methanol to the zinc nitrate hexahydrate in a glass vial; allow dissolution.
Add the other half of the methanol to 2-methylimidazole in another glass vial; allow dissolution.
Combine the two dissolved solutions into one container.
Place the combined solution on a stir plate and stir at 700 rpm for 24 hours at room temperature.
After 24 hours, transfer the reaction mixture to 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 3,075 x g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant from each tube after centrifugation.
Add methanol (5-15 mL) to the tubes and redisperse the particles.
Repeat the centrifugation and washing steps two to four more times.
After the final wash, remove the supernatant completely.
Remove the lids of the tubes and place parafilm tape over the top.
Poke holes in the parafilm.
Place the tube/s containing the sample in a vacuum chamber at room temperature to dry for 24 hours.
Mount the dry powders of ZIF-8 onto carbon tape.
Sputter for 120 seconds with gold-palladium.
Set the accelerating voltage of the microscope to 15 kV.
Bring the particles into focus and adjust the magnification.
Image the particles under magnifications ranging from 500x, 1,000x, 1,500x, 4,000x, 10,000x, 20,000x, 30,000x to 40,000x.
Collect data from at least three different fields of view and consider different magnifications for each.
Analyze the sample elemental composition using EDX spectroscopy.
Match the SEM accelerating voltage and magnification with the EDX monitor settings.
Turn off the infrared camera on the SEM microscope.
Go to Collect Spectrum on the EDX monitor.
Input a collection time of 200 seconds.
Collect data from at least three different fields of view.
Analyze the collected data.
Identify elements of interest in the analyzed data.
Culture immortalized BEAS-2B cells in media supplemented with 5% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 0.2% penicillin/streptomycin.
Place 10 mL of the media onto a 100 mm cell culture plate.
Add 1 mL of the BEAS-2B cell solution to the plate.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C in an atmosphere with 5% CO2.
Check the plate after 24 hours for 80% confluency.
Change the media if cells have not reached 80% confluency and continue incubation until they do.
Once cells reach 80% confluency, remove the media from the plate.
Wash the plate with 5 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Remove the PBS from the plate.
Add 2 mL of trypsin to the plate and place it in the incubator for 2 minutes.
Add 2 mL of media to the plate and pipette up and down to remove cells.
Transfer the solution to a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 123 x g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant from the tube and add 2 mL of media.
Pipette the media up and down to redisperse the cells.
Add 20 µL of trypan blue and then 20 µL of the cell solution (1:1 ratio) to a 1.5 mL tube.
Place 10 µL of the cell mixture onto a glass slide and place it onto an automatic cell counter.
Wait until the screen comes into focus, then select capture.
Count the number of cells in the four outer squares on the hemocytometer and divide by four.
Multiply the count by 10,000 to obtain the live cell count.
Add together the live and dead cell counts to obtain the total cell count.
Divide the live cell count by the total cell count to calculate viability.
Measure the amount of ZIF-8 and add deionized (DI) water to reach a 1 mg/mL concentration.
Sonicate the ZIF-8 stock solution for 2 min at 30 s intervals in a water bath.
Calculate the amount of ZIF-8 stock solution and DMEM needed for each dose using C1V1 = C2V2 equation.
Seed BEAS-2B cells at a density of 4 x 10^4 cells/mL in a 96-well plate with a volume of 100 μL/well.
Calculate the amount of cell solution needed to reach a density of 4 x 10^4 cells/mL using C1V1 = C2V2 equation.
Maintain blank wells for each dose by leaving them empty until ZIF-8 exposure.
Place the 96-well plate into the incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 to allow cells to grow to a confluent monolayer for 24 h.
Remove media from the wells after 24 h of growth.
Expose BEAS-2B cells to ZIF-8 doses ranging from 0-950 µg/mL by adding 100 μL of ZIF-8 to their respective blank and cell wells.
Place the 96-well plates back into the incubator for an exposure time of 48 h.
Add 10 μL of WST-1 to each well (blank and cell wells) after the exposure period.
Incubate the plate with WST-1 for 2 h.
Read changes in absorbance on a plate reader using a 485 nm wavelength.
Calculate the IC50 value through the software.
Use a 96-well plate (96W10idf) for ECIS analysis.
Place the 96-well plate onto the well station and click on the Setup button to test sensor connectivity.
Remove and reinsert the well plate, then click the Setup button again until all wells show green readings.
Stabilize electrodes for 40 min with 200 µL of media per well to prevent drift.
Add 200 µL of media to each well being used.
Place the 96-well plate onto the ECIS station and click on Setup/Check to ensure proper connection.
Click on Stabilize until stabilization is complete.
Remove the plate from the station and remove the media from each well.
Seed BEAS-2B cells at a density of 4 x 10^4 cells/mL with a volume of 100 µL per well into the wells containing the cells.
Place the seeded plate onto the ECIS station in the incubator.
On the monitor, click on Check to determine that all electrodes are read by the sensors on the station.
Set up the time course measurement by selecting Multiple Freq/Time (MFT).
Measure each well at seven different frequencies.
Click Start and allow it to run for 24 hours.
Pause the data collection after 24 hours when cells show increased resistance on the monitor.
Make ZIF-8 doses at, above, and below the calculated IC50 value following section 7 steps.
Expose ZIF-8 nanoparticles to their respective blank and cell wells with a volume of 100 μL per well.
Place the 96-well plate back onto the station.
Click on Check again on the monitor to ensure sensors are reading all electrodes.
Click on Resume and allow the system to run for 72 hours to monitor cellular behavior and attachment.
Once data collection has finished, click on Finish on the monitor.
To save the file, click File > Save As.
Save the data as a spreadsheet file.
Click on Model to get alpha parameters.
On the screen pop-up, click on Media-Only Well and select the well that has only media.
Click on Set Ref.
On the monitor, click on Find if the system shows an incorrect well.
If necessary, repeat step 9.16.
Once correct, click on Set.
Click on Fit T-Range to determine the time range desired for data collection.
Open the imaging software to analyze SEM images.
Click File > Open, and then select the image to analyze.
Click on Image > Type > 8 Bits to convert the image to grayscale to perform the threshold operation.
Calibrate the distance measurement of pixels to microns.
Click on the Straight-Line tool and trace the length of each particle aimed to be measured.
Click Analyze and then Set Scale. The known distance will be set to the length of the size of the scale bar on the SEM image. The known unit of length will be set to microns.
Check Global and press Ok.
Click on the Straight-Line tool and trace the diameter of the particle, then select Analyze and Measure.
Record the length result.
Repeat for all the collected images.
Average all the diameters from at least 60 particles for a suitable statistics evaluation.
Average all the weight percentages of each element together from all the collected images.
Using a spreadsheet, plot a bar graph of each element on the x-axis and their average elemental weight percentage on the y-axis.
Calculate the adjusted blank by subtracting the control blank average from the dose blank average.
Calculate the true cell value for each dose by subtracting the adjusted blank from the average dose value.
Subtract the adjusted blank value for each dose from the average control value.
Calculate the cell viability of each dose utilizing the equation: cell viability = (true cell value / (control value - adjusted blank value)) x 100.
Repeat this for all other replicates.
Average the cell viability for each replicate together to get the final cell viability for each dose.
Choose the XY tab in the software screen.
Enter the concentration (dose) values into the X column and the cell viability (%) from each dose into the Y column.
Transform the X values by clicking Analyze > Transform > Ok, and then selecting Transform X = Log(X).
Normalize the Y values by selecting the Transformed Data sheet, clicking on Analyze, and then selecting Normalize.
Select the Normalize of Transform data sheet, click Analyze, and select Nonlinear Regression (Curve Fit).
Select Dose-Response-Inhibition and click Log(Inhibitor) Vs. Response-Variable Slope (Four Parameters).
Click on OK to view the results.
Take the resistance (ohm) columns for each replicate (blank wells and dose wells) from the spreadsheet.
Average them together from the 4,000 Hz frequency.
Calculate the corrected resistance by subtracting the averaged blank from the averaged dose for each replicate.
Average the corrected resistance for the replicates for each dose.
Repeat the same steps to calculate the average alpha parameter.
Plot the x-axis as time (h) and the y-axis as the average resistance/alpha values for each dose value.
Calculate the standard deviation of the 60 ZIF-8 particles' diameters using the STDEV function in a spreadsheet.
Graph the standard deviation for each calculated average diameter.
Calculate the standard deviation for each average elemental composition using the STDEV function in a spreadsheet.
Graph the standard deviations for each average elemental composition.
Open the software utilized to calculate the IC50 and click on Grouped Data Sheet.
Enter the ZIF-8 doses in the rows labeled Group A, Group B, etc.
Enter the average cell viability for each dose and replicate in the corresponding column.
Click on Analyze and select One-way ANOVA (and nonparametric or mixed).
In the Experimental Design tab, select No Matching Or Pairing.
Under Gaussian Distribution Of Residuals, select Yes use ANOVA.
Finally, select Yes Use Ordinary ANOVA Test under Assume Equal SDs.
